paragraphs.source_en: The enemy was numerous, and besides, I had never seen such persons in this neighborhood before. Their beaks were queerly pointed, as though they were some godchild of a tengu; they certainly could not be creatures of good quality. Retreat would be the safest course; if I pushed too far and by some chance fell, the disgrace would be all the greater. Just as I was thinking this, the fellow who had turned to the left cried, “Fool!” The second imitated him and cried, “Fool!” And the one at the rear, with excessive politeness, troubled himself to cry twice, “Fool! Fool!” Though I am ordinarily mild-tempered, this was something I could not lightly overlook. If I were insulted by crows within my own estate, it would touch my good name. If one says that, since I have no name yet, there is no good name to touch, then it touches my dignity. I absolutely could not retreat. There is, after all, the proverb about a disorderly flock of crows; though there were three of them, they might prove unexpectedly weak. Resolving to advance as far as I could and yield not an inch, I began to walk forward at a slow, deliberate pace. The crows still wore an air of indifference, seeming to be talking among themselves. This stirred my temper all the more. Had the top of the bamboo fence been five or six inches wider, I would certainly have made them suffer; regrettably, however angry I grew, I could do no more than edge forward slowly. At last I came within some five or six inches of the foremost crow and thought one more effort would do it, when the three Kan-zaemons, as if by prior agreement, suddenly beat their wings and rose one or two feet into the air. The wind from their wings suddenly struck my face; I started, missed my footing, and dropped to the ground with a thud. Thinking I had made a mess of it, I looked up from beneath the fence, and there were all three crows still perched in their old place, their beaks aligned as they looked down at my face. What impudent creatures they were. I glared at them fiercely, but it had no effect at all. I arched my back and gave a low growl; that was still more useless. Just as common people fail to understand a subtle symbolic poem, so they showed no response whatever to the signs of anger I displayed toward them. On reflection, this was not unreasonable. Until then I had been treating them as though they were cats, and that was my mistake; had they been cats, such anger from me would certainly have told upon them. Unfortunately, my opponents were crows. Since they were those detestable crow fellows, there was nothing to be done. It was as helpless a matter as businessmen hurrying to overwhelm my master Kushami, as presenting a silver image of myself to the priest Saigyo, or as a crow dropping dung on the bronze statue of Mr. Saigo Takamori. Quick as I am to read the occasion, I perceived that it was utterly hopeless and withdrew cleanly, without regret, to the veranda. By then it was already time for supper. Exercise is all very well, but one must never overdo it.

paragraphs.source_zh: 敌人人多势众，而且在这一带我也没有见过它们，它们的嘴长得尖尖的，就好像是神赐给“天狗”的孩子那样，长着奇形怪状的尖嘴，肯定都不是好东西！退却乃万全之策，如果事情闹大了，万一我摔了下去，那就更丢人啦。我正在这样寻思，那扭头向左的家伙叫了声“傻瓜”，第二个也跟着叫了声“傻瓜”，而最后边的那个家伙更是多蒙它费神连叫了两声“傻瓜！傻瓜！”虽然我一向温厚，不过这次我可不能轻易饶过它们。如果在我的邸内竟然受此侮辱，这会有损于我的大名。如果说因为我至今还没有名字，不会损及我的大名，那么也会有损于我的体面。我决不能退却！俗语说“乌合之众”嘛，别看它们是三个，说不定都是些意想不到的软骨头。我横下心来，能前进多少就前进多少，决不退让，于是我慢条斯理地向前走去。乌鸦们仍表现出若无其事的样子，似乎在相互说话。这愈发惹起我的肝火。这竹墙顶的宽度如果再宽上五六寸，我肯定会让它们吃点苦头的，遗憾的是，不管我怎样发火，也只能慢慢地向前挪步。我好不容易离先头的乌鸦只差五六寸距离了，我想再加把劲就行了，就在这时，这三个勘左卫门就像事先商量好了的一般，猛地扑扇着翅膀，飞起一二尺高。它们扇起的风突然刮到我的脸上，我大吃一惊，一下子踩歪了，咚地摔到了地面上。我想这可糟了，我抬头从墙根向上一看，那三只乌鸦仍然停在原来的地方，一起伸着尖嘴向下看我哩。真是群胆大妄为的东西！我狠狠地瞪眼望着它们，可毫无用处。我拱起腰来稍稍发出怒声，这更不顶用。正像俗人不懂得灵妙的象征诗一般，它们对我发出的愤怒信号，没有任何反应。仔细想来，这也难怪。我适才是一直把它们作为猫儿同样看待的，这当然是个错误，如果对方也是猫儿，我这样愤怒相对，对方当然受不了。可不巧，对方是乌鸦。既然它们是一群乌鸦讨厌鬼，那又有什么办法呢。这就和实业家急于压倒我的主人苦沙弥一样，和赖朝将军将一只银制的猫儿的雕像送给了西行法师一样，和乌鸦在西乡隆盛君的铜像上脱粪一样，都是毫无办法的事。善于见机行事的我，已经认识到自己到底是无能为力，于是便毫无留恋地回到了廊子里。这时已经是吃晚饭的时候了。运动固然需要，但是决不能过度啊。
